question.text: Per Chapter 9, a Cat II AIF buys SRs of XYZ ARC. XYZ ARC is itself an investee of the same AIF. Is this transaction permitted?

answer.text: Yes, as long as both are in the same category.
Yes, with a related-party-transaction disclosure only.
NO — Chapter 9 explicitly states an AIF cannot invest in SRs issued by an ARC which is its portfolio investee company.
Yes, if the AIF has more than 100 investors.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'an AIF cannot invest in SRs issued by an ARC which is its portfolio investee company.' This is an absolute prohibition aimed at preventing conflict of interest — the AIF would otherwise be buying paper from its own portfolio company, creating circular valuation and disclosure problems. The Trap: Options A, B, D all try to create exceptions that do not exist — this is a bright-line prohibition. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) covers RPT frameworks in detail. XIX-A tests this at distributor level. XIX-C all-cat covered it. Manager's Pro-Tip: Bake this check into the pre-trade compliance layer. Conflict screens should cover not just the AIF's investee list but also associate/group company loans (the second bright-line prohibition).
